Speaker: Narration
Dialogue: The darkness has no end and no direction. Time itself has long since lost all meaning.

Speaker: Narration
Dialogue: The man can no longer feel his hands or feet. His body is weightless, sinking slowly through an endless silence.

Speaker: Narration
Dialogue: Just as his consciousness begins to flicker out, a touch of warmth reaches him before any voice does.

Speaker: Narration
Dialogue: Two small arms close around him, holding him so tightly that it seems one more squeeze might keep even death from pulling them apart.

Speaker: Girl
Dialogue: Dad!! Don't go!

Speaker: Narration
Dialogue: The man lowers his head.

Speaker: Narration
Dialogue: The girl's face is buried against his chest, her shoulders trembling without pause. It is the face that never came to him through the sleepless nights, no matter how tightly he closed his eyes.

Speaker: Narration
Dialogue: Then another voice rises from deeper in the darkness.

Speaker: Mom
Dialogue: I know everyone has to say goodbye someday.

Speaker: Mom
Dialogue: But it shouldn't be today... Not yet.

Speaker: Mom
Dialogue: So please. Don't go so far away on your own.

Speaker: Narration
Dialogue: He knows that voice.

Speaker: Narration
Dialogue: His wife stands behind the girl with one hand outstretched. She looks as she once did, before all those weary days and sleepless nights settled behind her eyes.

Speaker: Narration
Dialogue: They are so close.

Speaker: Narration
Dialogue: The man forces his stiffened arms upward, trying to gather them both against him.

Speaker: Narration
Dialogue: The instant his fingertips are about to touch them—

Speaker: Narration
Dialogue: Icy water rushes into his mouth and nose.

Speaker: Narration
Dialogue: The dream shatters.

Speaker: Narration
Dialogue: His lungs convulse from lack of air, his chest heaving uselessly. The man opens his eyes. Muddy water roars past, carrying broken branches and silt as it drags him ever deeper.

Speaker: Narration
Dialogue: Far above, the surface has dwindled to a small, blurred patch of gray-white light.

Speaker: Narration
Dialogue: The warmth is gone.

Speaker: Dad
Dialogue: ...So it was a dream.

Speaker: Dad
Dialogue: ...What a joke...

Speaker: Dad
Dialogue: I saw them both just a moment ago...

Speaker: Dad
Dialogue: But that's all it can ever be now. A dream that will never come true.

Speaker: Narration
Dialogue: His body continues to sink.

Speaker: Dad
Dialogue: After coming this far... after everything I've been through... is this really how it ends?

Speaker: Dad
Dialogue: I can't accept that.

Speaker: Dad
Dialogue: I don't want to die...

Speaker: Dad
Dialogue: I still haven't found her. What if she's somewhere out there, waiting for me...?

Speaker: Dad
Dialogue: At least...

Speaker: Narration
Dialogue: For the last time, the man raises one hand.

Speaker: Narration
Dialogue: His numb fingers slide inside his raincoat and find the folded missing-person flyer. The river has soaked the paper through, and the girl's frosting-smeared smile is slowly washing away.

Speaker: Narration
Dialogue: His fingers uncurl.

Speaker: Narration
Dialogue: The flyer slips from his palm. The current catches it and carries it away, toward a place he will never be able to follow.

Speaker: Narration
Dialogue: The man keeps watching it.

Speaker: Narration
Dialogue: Until the last faint glimmer of daylight fades from his eyes.

Speaker: SpecialNarration
Dialogue: Go on...

Speaker: SpecialNarration
Dialogue: Step into the unknown. Let death show you the way.

Speaker: SpecialNarration
Dialogue: Buy one more tomorrow for those you still love.

Speaker: Narration
Dialogue: The Old House on the Hill — Living Room.

Speaker: Narration
Dialogue: The front door is still unlocked, just as the man asked before he left.

Speaker: Narration
Dialogue: The woman sits beside the phone, the receiver pressed tight to her ear. With every long ring before the call connects, her breathing quickens.

Speaker: Dispatcher
Dialogue: 911. What's your emergency?

Speaker: Mom
Dialogue: My husband hasn't come home.

Speaker: Mom
Dialogue: He went out last night to look for our daughter. He said he was only going to check a lead downriver. Now I can't reach him, and no one by the levee has seen him.

Speaker: Mom
Dialogue: Please... help me find him.

Speaker: Dispatcher
Dialogue: Ma'am, please try to stay calm. How many people are you reporting missing?

Speaker: Mom
Dialogue: Two.

Speaker: Mom
Dialogue: No... there was only one at first.

Speaker: Mom
Dialogue: My husband went to find her. So now... there are two.

Speaker: Mom
Dialogue: My daughter, and her father.

Speaker: Narration
Dialogue: The dispatcher begins asking for their names, what they were wearing, when they left, and everywhere they might have gone.

Speaker: Narration
Dialogue: The woman answers each question.

Speaker: Narration
Dialogue: She remembers everything about them with perfect clarity.

Speaker: Narration
Dialogue: After the call, she returns to the entryway and places two pairs of slippers side by side.

Speaker: Narration
Dialogue: One large.

Speaker: Narration
Dialogue: One small.

Speaker: Narration
Dialogue: Their toes point inward, as though their owners might open the door at any moment and come home from the long night of rain.

Speaker: Narration
Dialogue: The entryway light burns all night.

Speaker: Narration
Dialogue: Beneath it, only her shadow remains.
